about.title: San Diego Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Diego moves on freeways. I-5 and I-805 carry much of the daily flow through the city, while El Cajon Boulevard and University Avenue thread through the neighborhoods east of Balboa Park. Those four corridors also appear most often in the public collision counts for this area. In 2025, the city recorded 5,813 injury collisions, and 7,830 people were hurt; 87 lost their lives. The busiest window for reported crashes falls on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m., when the week's traffic finally lets out. If one of those numbers now describes your afternoon, the days that follow can feel scattered. Adjusters call before the soreness sets in. Repair estimates arrive. Paperwork asks questions you are not sure how to answer. LawProactive exists to take one item off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent San Diego-area personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers something.

whyChoose.title: Why San Diego Drivers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: The clock in California is real
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but if a city truck or a Caltrans vehicle was involved, the window to file a government claim can shrink to six months. Getting connected early keeps those deadlines in view.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you share some blame; your share simply reduces the amount. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: Full value, no fee unless you recover
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and lost enjoyment of life in an ordinary car accident case. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, so nothing comes out of your pocket up front.

items.question: Does it matter that my crash happened on I-5 rather than a San Diego city street?
items.answer: For the fault rules and the general two-year filing period, the road itself does not change much. Where it can matter is if a public entity played a role, such as a city-owned vehicle or a road maintenance issue, because a claim against a government body in California often must be filed within six months. An attorney can sort out who is actually responsible and which deadline applies before anything lapses.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give the other insurer a recorded statement, and most attorneys will advise against it. Answers given while you are still sore or shaken can be used later to minimize your claim. It is reasonable to say you will respond once you have spoken with an attorney.

items.question: What should I hold onto after a car accident in San Diego?
items.answer: Keep photos of the vehicles, the roadway, and your injuries, along with the police report number and the other driver's information. Save every medical bill, work note, and text or email from an insurer. If a dashcam or nearby business camera captured the crash, ask about it quickly, since footage on El Cajon Boulevard or University Avenue storefronts is often overwritten within days.
